v06-caves-madeleine.name: Caves Madeleine
tags: Bistrot with the bones of a wine cellar — shared tables
v06-caves-madeleine.why: Bistrot with the bones of a wine cellar — shared tables. To order: hanger-steak tartare with hazelnut and Parmesan; the producer-sourced plat du jour. Long communal tables, wine bought off the shelf at retail-plus, kitchen that cooks with real punch. Closed Wed and Sun.
v06-caves-madeleine._lane: Wine rooms — the bistrots where the bottle comes first

v10-le-comptoir-des-tontons.name: Le Comptoir des Tontons
v10-le-comptoir-des-tontons.why: Bistrot-épicerie — natural and biodynamic wine. To order: the seasonal organic market plates; taste a wine, then buy the bottle off the shelf. A small room of natural-wine conviction on the Madeleine faubourg. Reserve — there are not many seats.
v10-le-comptoir-des-tontons._lane: Wine rooms — the bistrots where the bottle comes first

v11-enstase.name: Enstase
tags: Cave à manger — the natural-wine address of Beaune
v11-enstase.why: Cave à manger — the natural-wine address of Beaune. To order: natural wine, cider and kefir; Thursday and Friday the kitchen opens — bao and elaborate small plates. A room built entirely of natural materials, a low-intervention wine list, and a kitchen that wakes up at the week's end. The counter where young Beaune drinks.
v11-enstase._lane: Wine rooms — the bistrots where the bottle comes first

v15-march-des-halles-saturday.name: Marché des Halles (Saturday)
tags: The Saturday market — around 180 stalls, a real local event
v15-march-des-halles-saturday.why: The Saturday market — around 180 stalls, a real local event. To order: Époisses and Cîteaux cheese; jambon persillé; Fallot mustard from the stand; autumn girolles. 07:00–13:00 across Place de la Halle, Place Fleury and the covered halls. Saturday is the big one; Wednesday is the quieter, food-only market. Producers down from the hill villages.
v15-march-des-halles-saturday._lane: La Rue — the Saturday market, the charcutier and the pâtissier

v-charcuterie-raillard.name: Charcuterie Raillard
v-charcuterie-raillard.verdict: Eddy Raillard's charcuterie on rue Monge: the jambon persillé the critic Gilles Pudlowski called a model of the genre, with gougères and pâté en croûte, sold by the slice to eat standing up.
v-charcuterie-raillard.signature: A thick slice of jambon persillé, with bread and a cornichon.
v-charcuterie-raillard._source: old producer, street-food and eat cards
v-charcuterie-raillard._lane: La Rue — the Saturday market, the charcutier and the pâtissier

v16-p-tisserie-fabien-berteau.name: Pâtisserie Fabien Berteau
v16-p-tisserie-fabien-berteau.why: The pâtisserie address of Beaune. To order: the seasonal-fruit cheesecake, the chef's signature; macarons; the morning viennoiserie. Revised French classics and house-made ice cream. The tea room Le Garden opposite does an affordable lunch under a shaded summer terrace. Closed Wednesday.
v16-p-tisserie-fabien-berteau._lane: La Rue — the Saturday market, the charcutier and the pâtissier
